newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian scientists count 600 fires since March.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian scientists count 600 fires since March.

text.p: Indonesian scientists have counted at least 600 forest fires in the archipelago since March, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.
"Most of the fires are in Sumatra and Kalimantan," the deputy head of the National Outerspace and Aviation Agency (LAPAN), Mahdi Kartasasmita, was quoted as saying.
He said the agency's satellite images showed the worst fires were in the provinces of Riau on Sumatra as well as South and West Kalimantan on Borneo island.
Slash and burn farming techniques have been blamed for the fires.
Smoke from the fires has disrupted air and sea traffic on Sumatra and Kalimantan and has drifted across the Malacca Straits to peninsula Malaysia and Singapore.
